title: Systray's "back" animation should be sliding instead of crossfade
line: Going back from an applet to the System Tray's item grid now slides the grid in, like opening an applet does.
explanation: The tray popup shows the applet in a StackView, so opening one slides it in, but the grid of hidden items is a separate view that is simply made visible again when you press Back. So going back was an instant swap in which only the item labels faded in, which reads as a crossfade. The change runs a slide-and-fade on the grid when the active applet is cleared while the popup stays open, with the same distance, duration and easing as the StackView pop transition (mirrored for right-to-left).

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: slide back to the item grid when going back

Going back from an applet to the grid of items swapped the views at once
with only the labels fading in, while opening an applet slides it in.
Now the grid slides in from the side like a StackView pop transition.

BUG: 459201

media.caption: Master: Notifications slides in, but Back swaps straight to the grid with only the labels fading in (twice)
With the fix: Back slides the grid in from the left (twice)
Frames right after pressing Back on master: the grid is already in place, only labels fade
Frames right after pressing Back with the fix: the grid slides in from the left while fading in

reviews.text: Adding a mirrored slide-and-fade animation on HiddenItemsView when returning from an applet cleanly matches the StackView transition direction and timing without risking layout regressions from moving the grid into the StackView. Two polish/soundness issues remain: the translated grid overflows past its margin into the popup dialog's frame padding during the slide (visible in after-2.png frames 1-2), and backAnimation is not completed or reset if the grid is hidden or the popup is closed mid-animation.
changes: Clip the sliding HiddenItemsView (e.g., via a clipping wrapper Item around HiddenItemsView in ExpandedRepresentation.qml) so it does not draw over the dialog's left/right frame padding during the slide.

Complete or stop-and-reset backAnimation (restoring hiddenItemsViewTranslate.x = 0 and hiddenItemsView.opacity = 1) when hiddenItemsView becomes invisible or systemTrayState.expanded becomes false, so closing the popup or opening an applet mid-animation cannot leave a suspended or partial animation for the next open.
